IDEA: BEABLATE-CURVSCALE-RQ  (behaviour-demand offset measured through curved soft assignment, expressed in curved distance units; level-1 only)
TITLE: Level-1 curved assignment shifted by a mean-normalised, curved-metric behaviour-demand offset computed from the curved soft assignment itself.
MOTIVATION: RQ-VAE level-1 codes are chosen by nearest-Euclidean-residual only, so items that are behaviourally hot (many distinct outgoing transitions in the training split) and items that are behaviourally dead can land in the same top code, and the top prefix then carries no behavioural information for the generator. The generator's prefix tokens are the level-1 tokens, so level 1 is where a behaviour signal is worth the most. A flat offset that is not expressed in the same metric as the distance cannot express how strong "hot" is relative to how far apart codes are, and its effect silently changes when curvature changes.
NOVELTY: Differs from the four rejected arms (cross-graph two-segment transport, capacity cells, per-codeword curvature field, hierarchical curvature+Sinkhorn) and from the earlier issued rounds in two implementation-level ways that matter computationally: (1) the behaviour demand m_k is a soft-assignment statistic where the soft assignment is p_ik = softmax_k(-d_c(u_i,q_k)/mean_k d_c(u_i,q_k)), i.e. the behaviour statistic is measured with the curved distance, so geometry enters the behaviour measurement and behaviour enters the curved argmin — a two-way, single-pathway coupling rather than a behaviour term added beside a Euclidean statistical estimate; (2) the offset is multiplied by a measured per-step scale s_D (mean nearest-code curved distance in the batch), so off_k lives in curved-distance units and the behaviour/geometry balance is a fixed fraction of a typical distance instead of a curvature-dependent quantity (without s_D, changing c rescales d_c and confounds the behaviour-off vs geometry-off comparison).
CHANGE: In level 1 only, map the scale-normalised residual into the Poincare ball, score baseline codewords with the Poincare distance, and assign k_1 = argmin_k (D_k - w*s_D*log(clip(demand_k))). Demand is a frozen (no-grad) mean-normalised EMA of out-transition mass attributed to level-1 codes through the curved soft assignment; levels 2-3, the loss, the reconstruction codeword and the STE are exactly the baseline.
SPECIFICATION:
  Conventions (copied from the geometry contract): kappa = -c, c > 0, ball radius R_c = 1/sqrt(c); d_c(x,y) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh(sqrt(c) * ||(-x)(+)y||); exp_0^c(v) = tanh(sqrt(c)||v||) * v / (sqrt(c)||v||); the Euclidean norm of a tangent vector is NOT the Riemannian norm (||v||_{0,c} = 2||v||), so all offsets below are added to a distance (a length), never to a squared distance or a dot product.
  Scale: s = RMS of the level-1 latent residual over the training split, measured once on a frozen encoder forward pass over the train split, stored as a float, never updated.
  Derived curvature (not tuned): normalised residual x = r/s has RMS 1, set the ball radius to twice that scale, R_c = 2 => sqrt(c) = 1/2 => c = 0.25 in normalised units. This keeps sqrt(c)||u|| ~ 0.23 for a typical item, far from the boundary.
  Level 1 forward: u = exp_0^c(x); q_k = exp_0^c(a_k) with a_k the baseline (untrained-further) level-1 codebook row; D_k = d_c(u, q_k).
  Behaviour demand (frozen, no grad, training split only): with n_ij the directed transition counts of the train split, out-mass b_i = sum_j n

_ij; per step, p_ik = softmax_k(-D_ik / mean_k D_ik) (detached); mass_k = sum_{i in batch} p_ik * b_i / max(sum_{i in batch} p_ik, eps); m_k <- (1 - lambda) m_k + lambda * mass_k, m init 1.0, lambda = 1/72000 (one e-fold over the frozen 72000-step budget, a documented default, not tuned); demand_k = m_k / mean_k(m_k), so mean_k demand_k = 1 exactly each step.
  Offset and assignment: g_k = log(clip(demand_k, e^-1, e^1)); s_D = mean_i min_k D_ik over the batch; off_k = w * s_D * g_k with w = 0.25 (same order as the commitment weight, documented default); k_1 = argmin_k (D_k - off_k), ties -> smallest k. Since mean_k g_k ~ 0 off is a genuine zero-mean shift, and the bound |g_k| <= 1 makes |off_k| <= 0.25 * s_D, i.e. at most a quarter of a typical nearest-code distance.
  Switches (must exist, correct, never exercised in this round): use_behaviour=False => m_k held at 1.0 => demand_k = 1 => g_k = 0 => off_k = 0 => pure curved argmin; use_curvature=False => sqrt(c) -> 0 => D_k = 2||u - q_k|| with u = x, q_k = a_k (Euclidean argmin), p_ik uses those distances, s_D is the Euclidean nearest-code mean, everything else identical.
  Gradients: D_k, p_ik, m_k and off_k are all detached; they only move the argmin. The reconstruction still uses a_{k_1} exactly as the baseline uses a_{k_1}; the encoder gradient is the baseline identity STE dx/dr = 1/s plus the unchanged commitment term. No new loss term, no auxiliary hyperbolic loss.
COST: Per step at the frozen scale: one exp map on B x d, one Mobius add + artanh on B x K1 x d for D_k, one exp map on K1 x d for q_k, one scatter-add over K1 for the EMA. With documented defaults B = 256, K1 = 256, d = 32 this is ~2e7 MACs and ~B*K1 = 65k artanh evaluations per step, under ~2% of step wall-clock; over 72000 steps roughly minutes of extra GPU time on four cards. One-time: O(#train transitions) graph build (tens of seconds), one frozen encoder pass for s, K1 extra floats for m. Memory: K1 floats + one B x K1 detached matrix.
HYPOTHESIS: Hot level-1 neighbourhoods should stop sharing a top code with dead ones, so the level-1 prefix becomes more predictable and the generator's first token carries behaviour, which should show up as a higher Stage3 test_recall@10 than the 0.0555 baseline and clear 0.065. Observed as: (i) Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.065 in the single run; (ii) level-1 code-change rate vs the Euclidean baseline of order 5-20% of items, not 0% and not >50%; (iii) level-1 usage entropy roughly preserved (no code collapse); (iv) higher successor-share-level-1-code rate on the validation split as a recorded diagnostic only.
RISKS: The offset may swamp the distance and collapse level-1 onto a few hot codes (usage entropy drops), destroying the prefix tree; the EMA may be dominated by a handful of super-hot items so demand is a near-binary mask; s_D may be noisy for small batches so the offset jitters step to step; the level-1 decision boundary may move without any gradient reaching the encoder, so the effect is purely a reassignment that the levels 2-3 quantiser then partly compensates, giving a flat recall; the fixed c = 0.25 may put the codebook near the ball boundary for large residual outliers (mitigated by the radius clamp); the single run's seed noise may hide a real but small effect.
BEHAVIOR SIGNAL: Directed item transitions of the training split, reduced to per-anchor out-transition mass b_i, then attributed to level-1 codewords through the curved soft assignment to give per-codeword behavio

ur demand demand_k.
BEHAVIOR COMPUTATION: From the train split only: count directed transitions n_ij between consecutive items in each training sequence (deduplicated per sequence so one sequence cannot flood the count), out-mass b_i = sum_j n_ij, min-max-free raw counts; per Stage-2 step, for the items in the batch, compute p_ik = softmax_k(-D_ik/mean_k D_ik) from the current curved distances, form mass_k = sum_i p_ik b_i / sum_i p_ik, update m_k by EMA with lambda = 1/72000, and return demand_k = m_k/mean_k(m_k). Detached, not backpropagated, not used in any loss.
LEAKAGE BOUNDARY: The transition graph and b_i are built exclusively from the training split; s is measured on the training split only; the EMA sees only training batches, because Stage 2 iterates training sequences and no validation or test interaction is ever loaded into this path. demand_k is a running statistic of training batches only and is never re-estimated at inference; at evaluation the frozen m_k from the end of Stage 2 is used, so no validation or test co-occurrence can reach the SID construction. Nothing about the Stage-3 generator's target items enters level 1.
HYPERBOLIC OPERATOR: Fixed negative curvature Poincare ball, kappa = -c with c = 0.25 (sqrt(c) = 1/2, R_c = 2) in scale-normalised units, used as (a) the exponential map exp_0^c of both the residual and the codewords and (b) the Poincare distance d_c(u, q_k) = (2/sqrt(c))artanh(sqrt(c)||(-u)(+)q_k||); no trainable curvature.
HYPERBOLIC LOCATION: Quantisation only, at level 1 of the residual quantiser: it defines the level-1 distance that both the soft assignment statistic and the argmin are taken over. Levels 2 and 3 keep the baseline Euclidean residual recursion, distances, assignment and loss.
COUPLING PATH: One path: r -> x = r/s -> u = exp_0^c(x) -> D_k = d_c(u, exp_0^c(a_k)) -> {soft assignment p_ik used to build demand_k} and {offset off_k = w*s_D*log(clip(demand_k))} -> k_1 = argmin_k (D_k - off_k) -> recon codeword a_{k_1} -> baseline loss and STE -> encoder parameters. Removing behaviour sets off_k = 0 and removes the b_i weighting (m frozen at 1), which changes k_1; removing geometry replaces D_k by 2||u - q_k||, which changes both the offset scale s_D and the attribution p_ik as well as the argmin. Neither can be removed without changing k_1, and there is no second loss to hide in.
COUPLING EQUATION: k_1 = argmin_k [ d_c(u, exp_0^c(a_k)) - w * s_D * log(clip( m_k / mean_k(m_k), e^-1, e^1 )) ], with the demand m_k built from the same curved geometry via p_ik = softmax_k( -d_c(u_i, exp_0^c(a_k)) / mean_k d_c(u_i, exp_0^c(a_k)) ), i.e. behaviour term w*s_D*log(demand) and curved term d_c share one distance and one metric.
OBSERVABLES: Fraction of training and validation items whose level-1 code k_1 differs from the Euclidean-baseline assignment (target order 5-20%); level-1 code usage entropy and dead-code count; mean |off_k|/s_D (should sit below 0.25 by construction); successor-share-same-level-1-code rate on validation; level-1 commitment contribution; Stage3 test_recall@10 (the judgement, target > 0.065 vs baseline 0.0555).
ABLATION BEHAVIOR OFF: use_behaviour = False, so m_k stays 1.0, off_k = 0 exactly, and k_1 is the plain curved argmin; the run isolates what the behaviour demand contributes. Present in code, correct, not run in this round.
ABLATION GEOMETRY OFF: use_curvature = False, so c -> 0 and D_k = 2||x - a_k|| with u = x, q_k = a_k; p_ik, s_D and off_k are recomputed from the Eucli

dean distances, so the behaviour offset survives but lives in Euclidean units. Present in code, correct, not run in this round.
ABLATION BOTH ON: use_behaviour = True and use_curvature = True: the full coupled run described above, trained once, no early stopping, 3000 Stage-2 epochs, frozen Stage-3 protocol, single seed.
SPEC EQUATIONS:
  s = rms_train(||r||); x = r / s
  u = tanh(sqrt(c)||x||) * x / (sqrt(c)||x||)            (||x|| < eps -> u = x)
  q_k = tanh(sqrt(c)||a_k||) * a_k / (sqrt(c)||a_k||)
  d_c(u,q_k) = (2/sqrt(c)) * artanh(clip(sqrt(c)*|| mobius_neg(u) (+) q_k ||, 0, 1-1e-6))
  p_ik = softmax_k( -D_ik / (mean_k D_ik + eps) )         [detached]
  mass_k = sum_i p_ik * b_i / (sum_i p_ik + eps)          [detached]
  m_k <- (1-lambda) m_k + lambda * mass_k, m init 1, lambda = 1/72000
  demand_k = m_k / (mean_k m_k + eps)
  g_k = log(clip(demand_k, e^-1, e^1))
  s_D = mean_i (min_k D_ik)
  off_k = w * s_D * g_k, w = 0.25                          [detached]
  k_1 = argmin_k (D_k - off_k)                             [ties -> smallest k]
  z_1 = a_{k_1}; r_2 = r - z_1; levels 2,3 and loss unchanged; STE dx/dr = 1/s and identity pass-through as baseline
SPEC INPUTS OUTPUTS: Inputs: level-1 residual r (B x d), baseline level-1 codebook A (K1 x d), frozen scale s, frozen per-anchor out-mass b_i (N_train vector), running m (K1), curvature c, switches use_behaviour/use_curvature. Outputs: hard level-1 indices k_1 (B, int64), the quantised level-1 vector a_{k_1} identical to the baseline for the chosen index, the updated m (K1), and the detached diagnostics D (B x K1), off (K1), s_D (scalar) for logging. Nothing else in the model changes.
SAFEGUARDS: (1) exp map uses a Taylor branch u = x*(1 - c||x||^2/3) when sqrt(c)||x|| < 1e-4, avoiding 0/0. (2) Mobius addition argument clamped to [0, 1-1e-6] before artanh so no inf and finite gradient-free output. (3) s floored at 1e-6 and c fixed so sqrt(c)*||x|| stays far from 1 for the training RMS scale; s_D floored at 1e-6. (4) demand clipped to [e^-1, e^1] and m floored at 1e-6 before the log, so |off_k| <= 0.25*s_D by construction and a dead code cannot get an unbounded bonus. (5) m initialised at 1.0 so the first steps are behaviour-neutral and no code is starved before the EMA has seen a full pass. (6) softmax temperature is the per-item mean distance, not a free constant, so it cannot be tuned and is scale-free. (7) all assignment scores, p_ik, s_D and off_k are detached; they cannot inject a shortcut gradient into the encoder and cannot interact with the commitment weight. (8) deterministic tie-break and deterministic EMA order (batch order fixed by the frozen loader seed) for reproducibility. (9) if use_curvature = False the code path sets sqrt(c) = 0 and all length-like quantities fall back to the Euclidean formulas exactly, so the switch is a real branch, not a rescaling.
END IDEA
